# Ichikara - Full Context

> Generated by docmd

---

## [DSP Primitives](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/api/dsp/) (API)

---
title: "DSP Primitives"
description: "Low-level digital signal processing components"
---

## LFGlottalSource

Stateful LF glottal pulse source. Create one instance per voice and call `nextSample()` for each output sample.

```typescript
const glottal = new LFGlottalSource();

// Generate a single sample
const sample = glottal.nextSample({
  f0: 261.63,           // C4
  sampleRate: 44100,
  openQuotient: 0.5,
  speedQuotient: 0.85,
  tenseness: 0.55,
  aspiration: 0.05,
  power: 0.7,
  jitter: 0.015,
});

// Generate a buffer of samples
const buf = glottal.generate(params, 1024);

// Reset for a new phrase (avoids click from phase discontinuity)
glottal.reset();
```

## FormantFilter

Single biquad resonator or anti-resonator. Direct Form I implementation.

```typescript
const filter = new FormantFilter();

// Configure as resonator at 500 Hz with 100 Hz bandwidth
filter.setResonator(500, 100, 44100);

// Or as anti-resonator (zero)
filter.setAntiResonator(500, 100, 44100);

// Bypass (passthrough)
filter.setPassthrough();

// Process samples
const output = filter.processSample(input);
const buffer = filter.process(inputBuffer);

// Reset state
filter.reset();
```

## FormantCascade

Cascade of anti-resonators followed by resonators, modelling the vocal-tract transfer function. Typically 5 formants.

```typescript
const cascade = new FormantCascade(5); // 5 formants

// Set formant targets (all at once)
cascade.setFormants([
  { f: 730, bw: 90 },
  { f: 1090, bw: 120 },
  { f: 2440, bw: 150 },
  { f: 3500, bw: 200 },
  { f: 4500, bw: 300 },
], 44100, [{ f: 350, bw: 100 }]); // optional anti-formants

// Process
const out = cascade.processSample(inSample);

// Reset at phoneme boundaries
cascade.reset();
```

## interpolateFormants

Smooth (smoothstep) interpolation between two formant target arrays.

```typescript
const start = [{ f: 730, bw: 90 }, { f: 1090, bw: 120 }, /* ... */];
const end =   [{ f: 390, bw: 60 }, { f: 1990, bw: 80 }, /* ... */];

// t = 0 -> start, t = 1 -> end
const midway = interpolateFormants(start, end, 0.5);
```

## NoiseSource

Uniform white noise generator.

```typescript
const noise = new NoiseSource();
const buf = noise.generate(1024);
```

## shapeNoiseWithFormants

Shape white noise through a series of resonator filters.

```typescript
const noise = new NoiseSource().generate(1024);
const shaped = shapeNoiseWithFormants(noise, [
  { f: 4000, bw: 1000 },
  { f: 7000, bw: 2000 },
], 44100);
```

## applyAmplitudeEnvelope

Apply smooth attack/release envelope to a buffer (in-place).

```typescript
const buf = new Float32Array(44100);
applyAmplitudeEnvelope(buf, 1000, 5000); // 1000 samples attack, 5000 release
```

## mixBuffers

Additively mix a source buffer into a target buffer (in-place).

```typescript
mixBuffers(target, source, targetOffset, 0.5); // mix at 50% gain
```

## encodeWav

Encode AudioChunks as a 16-bit PCM WAV file.

```typescript
const wavBuffer: ArrayBuffer = encodeWav(chunks, 0.8); // 80% gain
```

## [Import / Export](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/api/import-export/) (API)

---
title: "Import / Export"
description: "Native projects and score conversion through UtaFormatix."
---

## Native projects and whole songs

Use `parseProject` and `serializeProject` for `.ichi` files. They retain native
voices, mix settings, region boundaries, and expression. See
[Native projects](projects.md) for examples.

For other score formats, `importProjectFromFile(file, language, id)` reads all
tracks. `exportProjectToBytes(project, { format: "ustx" })` exports the whole
song with absolute note placement. Score conversion cannot retain every native
field; imported tracks become one part each.

The single-score functions below select one track on import. Use them when your
app works with `Score` rather than `Project`.

## Score import

Import scores from any supported file format. The import pipeline:

```text
File or bytes  -->  utaformatix-3 parser  -->  UfData  -->  Score
```

### Supported Formats

| Extension            | Format                  | Import | Export |
|----------------------|-------------------------|--------|--------|
| `.ust`               | UTAU Sequence Text      | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.ustx`              | OpenUtau USTX           | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.vsqx`              | Vocaloid SQ             | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.vsq`               | Vocaloid SQ (legacy)    | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.vpr`               | Vocaloid 5 Project      | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.svp`               | SynthV Project          | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.s5p`               | SynthV S5P              | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.ccs`               | CeVIO Creative Studio   | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.dv`                | AHS VOICEROID           | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.mid` / `.midi`     | Standard MIDI           | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.musicxml` / `.xml` | MusicXML                | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.ppsf`              | Piapro Studio           | Yes    | No     |
| `.tssln`             | TSSLN                   | Yes    | Yes    |
| `.ufdata`            | UTAU Format Data (JSON) | Yes    | Yes    |

### Import from File

```typescript
import { importScoreFromFile } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

// Browser file input
const input = document.querySelector('input[type="file"]');
if (!(input instanceof HTMLInputElement)) throw new Error("Missing score file input");
input.addEventListener("change", () => {
  const file = input.files?.[0];
  if (!file) return;
  importScoreFromFile(file)
    .then((score) => console.info(`Imported ${score.notes.length} notes`))
    .catch((error: unknown) => console.error("Could not import score", error));
});
```

### Import from Bytes

```typescript
import { importScoreFromBytes } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const response = await fetch("song.ustx");
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Score download failed: ${response.status}`);
const buf = new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer());
const score = await importScoreFromBytes(buf, "song.ustx");
```

### Import Options

```typescript
const score = await importScoreFromFile(file, {
  trackIndex: 0,   // Import first track
  pitch: true,     // Include pitch-bend data
});
```

## Export

Export a Score to any supported format:

### Export as Bytes

```typescript
import { exportScoreToBytes } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const bytes = await exportScoreToBytes(score, {
  format: "ustx",
  projectName: "My Song",
});
```

### Export as Blob

```typescript
const blob = await exportScoreToBlob(score, { format: "mid" });
```

### Download in Browser

```typescript
import { downloadScore } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

await downloadScore(score, {
  format: "ustx",
  projectName: "exported-song",
});
```

### Low-Level: Direct UfData Conversion

```typescript
import { scoreToUfData, ufDataToScore } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const ufData = scoreToUfData(score);
const scoreBack = ufDataToScore(ufData);
```

## [API Reference](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/api/) (API)

---
title: "API Reference"
description: "Public types and functions for synthesis, projects, playback, and score conversion."
---

Import these types and functions from `@audiflo/ichikara`.

## Native projects

See [Native projects](projects.md) for document structure and examples.

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Project`, `VocalTrack`, `VocalPart`, `ProjectNote` | Song document types with stable IDs |
| `IdFactory`, `VoiceParameters`, `MeterEvent` | Host IDs, per-track voice controls, and meter changes |
| `createProject`, `addTrack`, `addPart` | Construct a song |
| `projectFromScore` | Wrap a single score in a native project |
| `validateProject`, `parseProject`, `serializeProject` | Validate and round-trip native JSON |
| `TempoMap`, `MeterMap` | Convert ticks, seconds, bars, and beats |
| `streamProject` | Render placed tracks and parts with a stereo mix |
| `importProjectFromFile`, `exportProjectToBytes` | Whole-song score conversion |
| `ufDataToProject`, `projectToUfData` | Direct UtaFormatix conversion |

## Core Types

| Export                | Description                                                             |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `VoiceConfig`         | Complete voice configuration (glottal, formant, vibrato, output format) |
| `GlottalConfig`       | LF glottal pulse source parameters                                      |
| `FormantConfig`       | Vocal-tract formant transformation                                      |
| `VibratoConfig`       | Pitch vibrato modulation                                                |
| `FormantTarget`       | Single formant centre frequency + bandwidth                             |
| `NoiseConfig`         | Noise source for consonant generation                                   |
| `PhonemeDef`          | Full acoustic definition of a phoneme                                   |
| `Note`                | A single note with lyric, pitch, timing, and overrides                  |
| `Score`               | Complete musical score (tempos + notes)                                 |
| `TempoEvent`          | Tempo change event                                                      |
| `AudioChunk`          | Processed audio segment with timeline position                          |
| `LanguageModule`      | Language module interface                                               |
| `PitchBend`           | Pitch-bend envelope                                                     |
| `GlottalSourceParams` | Runtime glottal source parameters                                       |

## DSP Primitives

| Export                   | Description                                  |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `LFGlottalSource`        | LF glottal pulse source (stateful)           |
| `FormantFilter`          | Biquad resonator / anti-resonator            |
| `FormantCascade`         | Cascaded formant filter bank                 |
| `interpolateFormants`    | Smooth interpolation between formant targets |
| `NoiseSource`            | White noise generator                        |
| `shapeNoiseWithFormants` | Filter noise through formant resonators      |
| `applyAmplitudeEnvelope` | Attack/release envelope shaping              |
| `mixBuffers`             | Additive buffer mixing                       |
| `encodeWav`              | Encode AudioChunks as WAV                    |

## Synthesis

| Export        | Description                     |
|---------------|---------------------------------|
| `renderNote`  | Render a single note            |
| `renderScore` | Render an entire score          |
| `streamScore` | Stream score as async generator |
| `mixChunks`   | Mix overlapping AudioChunks     |

## Language

| Export                | Description                           |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------|
| `getLanguage`         | Look up language module by ID         |
| `registerLanguage`    | Register a custom language module     |
| `japanese`            | Japanese language module              |
| `english`             | English language module               |
| `mandarin`            | Mandarin Chinese language module      |
| `toCanonical`         | Map phoneme symbol to canonical IPA   |
| `sequenceToCanonical` | Map phoneme sequence to canonical IPA |

## Voice

| Export          | Description                             |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `getVoice`        | Look up registered voice by name        |
| `registerVoice`   | Register a custom voice config          |
| `chitoseChika`    | Chitose Chika, the female voice          |
| `chitoseSho`      | Chitose Sho, the male voice              |
| `chitoseRen`      | Chitose Ren, the neutral voice           |
| `chitoseVoices`   | All named voices, in UI order           |
| `buildVoice`      | Build voice from partial overrides      |
| `scaleVoice`      | Scale voice along perceptual dimensions |

## Playback

| Export         | Description                                       |
|----------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `StreamPlayer` | Web Audio streaming player                        |
| `PlayerState`  | Player state type ("idle" / "playing" / "paused") |
| `PlayerEvent`  | Player event union type                           |
| `PlayOptions`  | Playback options                                  |

## Import / Export

| Export                 | Description                                          |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `ufDataToScore`        | Convert UfData (utaformatix-3 intermediate) to Score |
| `importScoreFromFile`  | Import score from a File object                      |
| `importScoreFromBytes` | Import score from raw bytes                          |
| `ImportOptions`        | Import options                                       |
| `UfData`               | UTAU Format Data structure                           |
| `scoreToUfData`        | Convert Score to UfData                              |
| `exportScoreToBytes`   | Export score as Uint8Array                           |
| `exportScoreToBlob`    | Export score as Blob                                 |
| `exportScoreToUrl`     | Export score as blob URL                             |
| `downloadScore`        | Trigger browser download                             |
| `ExportOptions`        | Export options                                       |

## [Native projects](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/api/projects/) (API)

---
title: "Native projects"
description: "Create, validate, save, and render multi-track Ichikara songs."
---

# Native projects

`Project` is the document behind an `.ichi` file. It contains the song's timing,
tracks, parts, notes, voices, and mix settings. It does not contain file handles,
audio resources, panel sizes, or other host-specific state.

## Create a song

IDs come from the host and must be unique throughout the document. Pass a
function that calls `crypto.randomUUID()` rather than an unbound browser method.

```typescript
import { createProject, addTrack, addPart, chitoseChika, serializeProject } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const id = () => crypto.randomUUID();
const project = createProject("Evening", id);
const track = addTrack(project, "Lead", chitoseChika, "jp", id);
const part = addPart(track, "Verse", 0, 1920, id);

part.notes.push({
  id: id(),
  tick: 0,
  length: 960,
  noteNum: 64,
  lyric: "あ",
  intensity: 100,
  pitchBend: { ticks: [0, 240, 960], values: [-0.5, 0, 0] },
});

const source = serializeProject(project);
```

`createProject` starts at 120 BPM, 4/4, and 480 ticks per quarter note.
`addTrack` and `addPart` append to their parent and return the new object.
`addTrack` clones the supplied base voice so tracks can be edited independently.

## Coordinates and fields

| Field                      | Meaning                                               |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `project.tempos`           | Absolute tick positions and BPM values                |
| `project.meters`           | Absolute tick positions, numerators, and denominators |
| `track.voice`              | Stored base voice configuration                       |
| `track.parameters`         | Per-track `scaleVoice` parameters                     |
| `track.gain`, `track.pan`  | Linear gain and pan from -1 (left) to 1 (right)       |
| `track.mute`, `track.solo` | Track playback and render selection                   |
| `part.tick`, `part.length` | Absolute start and duration in project ticks          |
| `note.tick`, `note.length` | Start relative to the part, and duration              |
| `note.pitchBend`           | Note-relative ticks and semitone offsets              |

`ProjectNote` extends `Note` with a required stable `id` and `tick`. A note's
absolute song position is `part.tick + note.tick`. Use `TempoMap` to convert
ticks and seconds, and `MeterMap` for bar/beat positions and grid lines.

## Validate and save

`serializeProject(project)` validates the document and returns JSON with a final
newline. `parseProject(source)` reads JSON and validates its fields and version.
Both throw for invalid documents; handle those errors at your file or UI boundary.
`validateProject(value)` also accepts unknown data and narrows it to `Project`.

The filename extension is `.ichi`; the JSON discriminator remains
`format: "ichikara"` and `version: 1`. Changing the extension does not change the
document schema. The editor still accepts the older `.ichikara` extension.

## Render the song

```typescript
import { streamProject, encodeWav, type AudioChunk } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const chunks: AudioChunk[] = [];
for await (const chunk of streamProject(project, 48000)) {
  chunks.push(chunk);
}
const wav = encodeWav(chunks);
```

`streamProject` yields stereo chunks in absolute sample order. It applies part
placement, track voice parameters, mute/solo, gain, and equal-power pan. The
default sample rate is 44100 Hz. Chunks may overlap; `encodeWav` mixes them.
An early iterator return closes the part producers. Validation, language, and
synthesis errors propagate to the caller.

## Convert other formats

`importProjectFromFile(file, language, id)` imports every track from a supported
score file. Each imported track gets a native part and host-generated IDs.
`exportProjectToBytes(project, { format: "ustx" })` exports all tracks using
absolute note positions.

For direct conversion, use `ufDataToProject(data, language, id)` and
`projectToUfData(project, options)`. Region boundaries, native voices, mix
controls, and some expression fields are not represented by UtaFormatix data.
Keep an `.ichi` copy when converting. See [Import / Export](import-export.md).


---

## [VoiceConfig Reference](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/api/voice-config/) (API)

---
title: "VoiceConfig Reference"
description: "Complete reference for all VoiceConfig parameters and their perceptual effects"
---

## Overview

`VoiceConfig` is the central configuration object passed to every render call. It bundles glottal source parameters, formant transformations, vibrato, and output format settings.

```typescript
interface VoiceConfig {
  name: string;
  glottal: GlottalConfig;
  formant: FormantConfig;
  vibrato: VibratoConfig;
  sampleRate: number;
  channels: 1 | 2;
}
```

## GlottalConfig (Glottal Source)

The glottal source generates the raw pulse train. Its parameters control the shape and stability of the vocal-fold oscillation.

```typescript
interface GlottalConfig {
  openQuotient: number;   // 0.2 - 0.9
  speedQuotient: number;  // 1.3 - 3.0 (see below for why the lower bound exists)
  tenseness: number;      // 0 - 1
  aspiration: number;     // 0 - 0.3
  power: number;          // 0 - 1
  jitter?: number;        // 0 - 0.05
}
```

### openQuotient

Fraction of the glottal cycle during which the vocal folds are open.

| Value | Perceptual Effect                       |
|-------|-----------------------------------------|
| ~0.3  | Pressed, tense voice (short open phase) |
| ~0.5  | Neutral, modal voice                    |
| ~0.7  | Breathy, soft voice (long open phase)   |
| >0.8  | Very breathy, almost whisper-like       |

Female voices typically use higher OQ (~0.52) than male voices (~0.4).

### speedQuotient

Ratio of the glottal opening duration to closing duration. Controls the skew of the glottal pulse.
It maps to `Tp = Te * sq / (1 + sq)`, the time of the glottal flow minimum within the open phase.

**Valid range is 1.3 and up.** The opening phase is
`E0 * exp(alpha*t) * sin(w_g*t)` with `w_g = pi/Tp`, so it sweeps `w_g*Te` radians over
the open phase. The LF model is only well posed while that sweep stays in `(pi, 2pi)`,
which means `Tp` must exceed `Te/2`, which means `sq` must exceed 1. At `sq = 0.5` and
`sq = 1` exactly, `sin(w_g*Te)` is zero and the amplitude `E0` diverges. Below 1 the
opening completes an extra whole cycle and the continuity equation has no real root.
Values under 1.22 are therefore clamped to the nearest valid configuration.

| Value | Perceptual Effect                     |
|-------|---------------------------------------|
| ~1.4  | Slowest valid closure, dark, rounded  |
| ~2.0  | Natural, balanced                     |
| ~2.5  | Brighter, crisper onset               |
| >3.0  | Very sharp closure, buzzy             |

### tenseness

Spectral tilt control. Higher values attenuate the high-frequency content of the glottal source.

| Value | Perceptual Effect                     |
|-------|---------------------------------------|
| ~0.2  | Very bright, thin (low spectral tilt) |
| ~0.5  | Neutral balance                       |
| ~0.7  | Dark, warm (higher spectral tilt)     |
| >0.8  | Very dark, muffled                    |

### aspiration

Amount of turbulence noise mixed into the glottal source. Simulates incomplete glottal closure.

| Value | Perceptual Effect                            |
|-------|----------------------------------------------|
| 0     | Clean, no audible aspiration                 |
| ~0.02 | Slight breathiness (natural for most voices)  |
| ~0.05 | Noticeably breathy                            |
| >0.1  | Very breathy, significant noise floor         |

The aspiration noise is low-passed at ~4 kHz to stay in the natural band. It is shaped by two resonators whose peak gain is several times the nominal amplitude, so values above ~0.05 add an audible hiss in the 3-4.5 kHz band. Keep named voices low and let `breathiness` scale up from there.

### power

Overall gain multiplier for the glottal pulse before formant filtering.

| Value | Perceptual Effect |
|-------|-------------------|
| ~0.5  | Quiet, soft       |
| ~0.7  | Moderate volume   |
| ~0.9  | Loud, full        |

Power interacts with the post-render normalisation: higher power produces a higher peak, which is then scaled back by the gain limiter.

### jitter

Random cycle-to-cycle variation in fundamental frequency and amplitude. Adds natural instability.

| Value | Perceptual Effect                                 |
|-------|---------------------------------------------------|
| 0     | Perfectly stable (robotic)                        |
| ~0.01 | Very slight natural variation                     |
| ~0.02 | Noticeable roughness (typical for natural voices) |
| >0.03 | Rough, hoarse                                     |

Both F0 jitter (frequency variation) and shimmer (amplitude variation) scale with this parameter.

## FormantConfig (Vocal Tract)

The formant config applies a global transformation to all phoneme formant targets. This is equivalent to changing the size or shape of the vocal tract.

```typescript
interface FormantConfig {
  scale: number;      // 0.5 - 2.0 (typically 0.8 - 1.2)
  shift: number;      // -12 - +12 semitones
  bandwidth: number;  // 0.5 - 2.0
}
```

### scale

Multiplicative scale factor on all formant centre frequencies. Simulates vocal-tract length scaling.

| Value | Perceptual Effect                              |
|-------|------------------------------------------------|
| ~0.8  | Larger vocal tract, darker, "more masculine"   |
| 1.0   | Neutral (no change)                            |
| ~1.2  | Smaller vocal tract, brighter, "more feminine" |
| ~1.5  | Very small vocal tract, "child-like"           |

A scale of 1.18 is used by the female voice preset to produce the typical female formant shift.

### shift

Additive formant shift in semitones, applied after scaling. Finer control than scale.

| Value | Perceptual Effect    |
|-------|----------------------|
| -6    | Darker, more muffled |
| 0     | Neutral              |
| +6    | Brighter, more nasal |

### bandwidth

Multiplier on all formant bandwidths. Controls the width of resonant peaks.

| Value | Perceptual Effect                    |
|-------|--------------------------------------|
| ~0.6  | Narrow resonances, ringing, "twangy" |
| 1.0   | Neutral                              |
| ~1.5  | Wide resonances, muffled, soft       |
| >2.0  | Very wide, formants blur together    |

## VibratoConfig (Pitch Modulation)

```typescript
interface VibratoConfig {
  rate: number;    // Hz (typically 4 - 7)
  depth: number;   // cents (typically 10 - 80)
  attack: number;  // seconds (0 - 2)
}
```

### rate

Frequency of the vibrato oscillation in Hz (cycles per second).

| Value | Perceptual Effect              |
|-------|--------------------------------|
| ~4    | Slow, wide vibrato (classical) |
| ~5.5  | Moderate vibrato (male pop)    |
| ~6    | Moderate vibrato (female pop)  |
| >7    | Fast, tremolo-like             |

### depth

Peak-to-peak depth of the pitch modulation in cents (100 cents = 1 semitone).

| Value | Perceptual Effect               |
|-------|---------------------------------|
| ~10   | Very subtle, barely perceptible |
| ~30   | Moderate vibrato                |
| ~50   | Wide, expressive vibrato        |
| >80   | Extreme, wobbling               |

### attack

Time in seconds for the vibrato to reach full depth after the note onset.

| Value | Perceptual Effect                  |
|-------|------------------------------------|
| 0     | Vibrato starts instantly           |
| ~0.1  | Quick onset (pop style)            |
| ~0.3  | Gradual onset (classical style)    |
| >0.5  | Late vibrato, note starts straight |

## Output Format

```typescript
sampleRate: number;  // 22050 - 96000 (typical: 44100)
channels: 1 | 2;     // 1 = mono, 2 = stereo
```

### sampleRate

Output sample rate in Hz. 44100 is the standard CD quality. Lower rates (22050) save CPU at the cost of high-frequency content.

### channels

- **1**: Mono output (single Float32Array per chunk)
- **2**: Stereo output (identical data in both channels)

## Voice Presets

The library ships with three named voices, one per register:

### Chitose Chika (female)

```typescript
{
  glottal: { openQuotient: 0.51, speedQuotient: 2.25, tenseness: 0.5, aspiration: 0.018, power: 0.66, jitter: 0.015, shimmer: 0.03 },
  formant: { scale: 1.16, shift: 0, bandwidth: 1.02 },
  vibrato: { rate: 5.9, depth: 38, attack: 0.11 },
}
```

### Chitose Sho (male)

```typescript
{
  glottal: { openQuotient: 0.42, speedQuotient: 2.7, tenseness: 0.66, aspiration: 0.009, power: 0.78, jitter: 0.012, shimmer: 0.025 },
  formant: { scale: 0.88, shift: -1, bandwidth: 0.92 },
  vibrato: { rate: 5.0, depth: 26, attack: 0.16 },
}
```

### Chitose Ren (neutral)

```typescript
{
  glottal: { openQuotient: 0.48, speedQuotient: 2.5, tenseness: 0.57, aspiration: 0.014, power: 0.7, jitter: 0.017, shimmer: 0.032 },
  formant: { scale: 0.97, shift: 0, bandwidth: 1.05 },
  vibrato: { rate: 5.6, depth: 32, attack: 0.14 },
}
```

`chitoseVoices` holds all three in that order.

## Perceptual Scaling

The `scaleVoice()` function maps high-level perceptual controls to the underlying parameters. Each control is a shift *away from the voice you pass in*, so the neutral point of every control returns that voice unchanged:

| Control         | Neutral | Range                                                              |
| --------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `gender`        | `0`     | `-1` masculine to `1` feminine                                     |
| `breathiness`   | `0.5`   | `0` no breath noise, `0.5` the voice's own aspiration, `1` doubled |
| `tension`       | `0.5`   | `0` relaxed, `1` pressed                                           |
| `brightness`    | `0.5`   | `0` dark, `1` bright                                               |
| `vibratoAmount` | `0.5`   | `0` none, `0.5` the voice's own depth, `1` doubled                 |

```typescript
const adjusted = scaleVoice(chitoseChika, {
  gender: 0.3,        // More feminine (formant scale + SQ)
  breathiness: 0.4,   // Increase OQ + aspiration
  tension: 0.6,       // Increase tenseness
  brightness: 0.7,    // Reduce formant bandwidth
  vibratoAmount: 0.8, // Scale vibrato depth
});
```

## Building Custom Voices

Use `buildVoice()` with partial overrides for a neutral starting point:

```typescript
const myVoice = buildVoice({
  name: "Custom",
  sampleRate: 48000,
  glottal: { openQuotient: 0.6, aspiration: 0.03 },
});
```

All unspecified fields fall through to neutral defaults.


---

## [Development checks](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/development/) (Development)

# Development checks

The library and editor extend `tsconfig.base.json`. Dependency declarations are
checked, including indexed access and exact optional properties. Browser and
worker code use separate compiler projects because DOM and WebWorker globals
cannot be loaded into the same TypeScript program.

Bits UI's generated declarations depend on CSS properties removed in `csstype`
3.2. The demo pins `csstype` to 3.1.3, matching Bits UI's build dependency, until
Bits UI regenerates those declarations against the newer CSS definitions.

## Commands

- `npm run typecheck` builds the library, then checks library source, tests,
  scripts, Svelte components, workers, and editor configuration.
- `npm run lint` runs type-aware strict ESLint without modifying files.
- `npm test` runs library and editor regression tests.
- `npm run check` runs the checks above and builds the production editor.
- `npm run lint:fix -w Build` or `-w Demo` applies ESLint's automatic fixes.

CI uses Node 22 and 24. Pages, npm releases, Updato, and the dependency audit use
Node 24. Use Node 22.18+ or 24.11+ locally to satisfy tsdown's runtime requirements
and support native type stripping for the editor's pure TypeScript tests.

The library's tsdown options live in the build command in `Build/package.json`.
Using its CLI avoids importing declarations for unused plugin integrations and
installing their optional bundlers. The build emits minified ESM and CommonJS,
declarations, and source maps. Source and dependency type checks remain strict.

## Dependency declarations

The root postinstall runs `Build/scripts/repair-declarations.mjs`. It preserves
runtime code and public prop types while repairing these published declarations:

- UtaFormatix 0.4.1 imports a nonexistent, unused `core.d.ts`.
- Bits UI 2.18.1 instantiates Svelte's `Component` with large prop unions.
  Computing its `keyof Props` binding constraint exceeds TypeScript's complexity
  limit. The repair spells out the same callable shape, including static members,
  legacy return members, typed `$set`, and exact binding names.

Repairs are idempotent and fail when their expected declaration changes. Review
them when updating dependencies. `skipLibCheck` remains disabled.

The Bits UI repair preserves literal `$$` binding markers and upgrades declarations
written by the earlier repair, which collapsed `$$` to `$`.


---

## [Core Concepts](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/getting-started/concepts/) (Getting Started)

---
title: "Core Concepts"
description: "Understand how Ichikara produces singing voice audio"
---

## Source-Filter Model

Ichikara implements the **source-filter model of speech production**: a glottal source (the "buzz" from the vocal folds) is shaped by a filter (the vocal tract's resonances). This separation lets you control pitch and timbre independently.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    G[Glottal Source<br/>LF model] --> F[Formant Cascade<br/>vocal tract] --> O[Output]
    G -.-> Gp[F0, OQ, SQ,<br/>tenseness,<br/>aspiration, jitter]
    F -.-> Fp[F1-F5 frequencies,<br/>bandwidths,<br/>antiformants]
```

The glottal source generates a periodic pulse train at the fundamental frequency (F0). The formant cascade applies a series of resonators (poles) and anti-resonators (zeros) to shape the spectrum into vowels and consonants.

## VoiceConfig

The `VoiceConfig` is the central configuration object. It bundles:

| Component    | Controls                                     | Perceptual Effect                             |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `glottal`    | OQ, SQ, tenseness, aspiration, power, jitter | Voice quality, breathiness, roughness         |
| `formant`    | Scale, shift, bandwidth                      | Vocal-tract size, brightness, resonance width |
| `vibrato`    | Rate, depth, attack                          | Pitch modulation (vibrato)                    |
| `sampleRate` | Output sample rate                           | Audio fidelity                                |
| `channels`   | Mono or stereo                               | Output format                                 |

See the [VoiceConfig reference](../api/voice-config.md) for detailed parameter documentation.

## Language Modules

Each language module provides:

- A **phoneme inventory** (Map of symbol -> acoustic definition)
- A **G2P converter** (lyric text -> phoneme symbol sequence)
- Optional **accent resolution** (pitch-accent patterns for prosody)

Built-in languages cover English (ARPAbet + CMUDict), Japanese (hiragana/romaji + EDICT2), and Mandarin (pinyin decomposition).

## Score and Rendering

A `Score` is a sequence of notes with a tempo map. The renderer:

1. Converts each note's lyric to phoneme symbols via the language module
2. Maps phoneme symbols to acoustic targets (formants, noise parameters)
3. Generates a glottal pulse train at the note's F0 (+ pitch bend + vibrato)
4. Filters through the formant cascade (with cross-phoneme interpolation)
5. Mixes in noise for consonants
6. Applies amplitude envelopes and normalisation

The output is an `AudioChunk` per note, carrying sample-accurate timeline positioning.

## Streaming

`streamScore()` returns an `AsyncGenerator<AudioChunk>`, producing one chunk at a time. This enables interleaved rendering and playback via `StreamPlayer`, which schedules chunks against the Web Audio clock with batching and buffer pooling.

---
title: "Installation"
description: "Install Ichikara via npm or use it directly in the browser"
---

## npm

The [browser editor](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara) needs no installation. To use
the synthesis library in another project:

```bash
npm install @audiflo/ichikara
```

## Browser (CDN)

```html
<script type="module">
  import { renderScore, chitoseChika } from "https://unpkg.com/@audiflo/ichikara/dist/index.mjs";
</script>
```

## Build from Source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Audiflo/Ichikara.git --recurse-submodules
cd Ichikara
npm ci
npm run build -w Build
npm run dev -w Demo
```

The `--recurse-submodules` flag is required for CMUDict (English G2P data).

## Requirements

- **Node.js 22.18+ or 24** for development and server-side examples
- **Any modern browser** (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) for browser usage
- No native dependencies - pure JavaScript/TypeScript

Run `npm run check` from the repository root for type checks, lint, tests, and a
production build. See [Development checks](../development.md) for compiler setup.

## [Quick Start](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/getting-started/quickstart/) (Getting Started)

---
title: "Quick Start"
description: "Render a phrase to WAV and play it in the browser."
---

This example renders a Japanese phrase with Chitose Chika and saves it as WAV.
For the browser editor, see the [song editor guide](../guide/editor.md).

::: callout tip "Prerequisites"
Use Node.js 22.18+ or 24 for the file example, or a modern browser for playback.
See [Installation](./installation).
:::

::: steps

1. **Create a Score**

   A Score is the input to the renderer: tempo map, timing resolution, and a list of notes. Each note has a lyric, MIDI note number, and duration.

   ```typescript
   import { renderScore, chitoseChika, encodeWav, type Score } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

   const score: Score = {
     tempos: [{ tick: 0, tempo: 120 }],
     resolution: 480,
     notes: [
       { lyric: "こ", noteNum: 60, length: 480 },
       { lyric: "ん", noteNum: 62, length: 480 },
       { lyric: "に", noteNum: 64, length: 480 },
       { lyric: "ち", noteNum: 65, length: 480 },
       { lyric: "は", noteNum: 67, length: 960 },
     ],
   };
   ```

   The lyric text is passed through the language module's G2P pipeline:
   - **Japanese**: hiragana / kanji -> romaji -> phoneme symbols
   - **English**: text -> CMUDict lookup -> ARPAbet phonemes
   - **Mandarin**: pinyin syllables -> initial + final decomposition

2. **Render the Score**

   Call `renderScore` with your score, a voice config, and a language identifier:

   ```typescript
   const chunks = await renderScore(score, chitoseChika, "jp");
   console.log(`Rendered ${chunks.length} notes`);
   ```

   Each chunk is an `AudioChunk` with sample-accurate positioning on the timeline. You can mix them into a single buffer or stream them to the audio output.

3. **Export as WAV**

   ```typescript
   const wav = encodeWav(chunks);
   // Node.js: save to disk
   const { writeFileSync } = await import("node:fs");
   writeFileSync("output.wav", Buffer.from(wav));
   ```

   Or in the browser, create a download link:

   ```typescript
   const blob = new Blob([wav], { type: "audio/wav" });
   const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
   const a = document.createElement("a");
   a.href = url;
   a.download = "output.wav";
   a.click();
   URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
   ```

4. **Stream to Audio Output (Browser)**

   For real-time playback without waiting for the full render:

   ```typescript
   import { streamScore, StreamPlayer } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

   const player = new StreamPlayer();
   await player.play(streamScore(score, chitoseChika, "jp"));
   ```

   The renderer produces audio chunks while the player schedules them against the Web Audio clock. Pre-buffer threshold defaults to 1 second.

5. **Try a Different Voice**

   Ichikara ships with three named voices, plus a builder for custom ones:

   ```typescript
   import { chitoseChika, chitoseSho, buildVoice, scaleVoice } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

   // Use a built-in voice
   const chunks1 = await renderScore(score, chitoseSho, "jp");

   // Build a custom voice
   const custom = buildVoice({ name: "My Voice", sampleRate: 48000 });

   // Scale along perceptual dimensions
   const breathy = scaleVoice(chitoseChika, {
     breathiness: 0.6,
     tension: 0.3,
     vibratoAmount: 0.5,
   });

   const chunks2 = await renderScore(score, breathy, "jp");
   ```

:::

## [Architecture](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/guide/architecture/) (Guide)

---
title: "Architecture"
description: "How the Ichikara library is organised"
---

## Module Layout

The library is organised into four layers:

```text
src/
  core/              - Data types + low-level DSP primitives
    types.ts         - VoiceConfig, Note, Score, PhonemeDef, etc.
    dsp/             - LF glottal source, formant filters, noise, envelope, WAV
  langs/             - Language modules (G2P, phoneme inventories)
    index.ts         - Registry + lookup
    english.ts       - ARPAbet + CMUDict G2P
    japanese.ts      - Hiragana/romaji + EDICT2 kanji G2P
    mandarin.ts      - Pinyin syllable decomposition
    alias.ts         - Cross-language canonical phoneme mapping
  synth/             - Rendering pipeline
    renderer.ts      - Single-note renderer
    stream.ts        - Score-level streaming + mixing
  voices/            - Voice presets and configuration
    index.ts         - chitoseChika, chitoseSho, chitoseRen, buildVoice, scaleVoice
  player/            - Web Audio playback
    stream-player.ts - AsyncGenerator consumption + AudioContext scheduling
  import/            - File import (utaformatix-ts based)
    ufdata.ts        - ufDataToScore, importScoreFromFile, importScoreFromBytes
  export/            - File export (utaformatix-ts based)
    ufdata.ts        - scoreToUfData, exportScoreToBytes, exportScoreToBlob, downloadScore
```

## Data Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    F[File: UST, MIDI, etc.] -->|importScoreFromFile<br/>importScoreFromBytes| S[Score]
    S -->|renderScore / streamScore| A["AudioChunk[]"]
    S -.-> VC[VoiceConfig]
    S -.-> LM[LanguageModule]
    A -->|encodeWav| W[WAV file]
    A -->|StreamPlayer.play| P[Audio output]
```

## Design Decisions

- **DSP is stateless per-note**: Each note render creates its own `LFGlottalSource` and `FormantCascade` instances. The only cross-note state is the last phoneme's formant targets, passed as `prevFormants` for smooth transitions.
- **Lazy G2P loading**: utaformatix-ts is loaded on first import/export call, keeping the initial bundle small.
- **No Web Audio dependency in the core**: The synth layer produces `AudioChunk` objects with no DOM or AudioContext dependency. Only `StreamPlayer` touches the Web Audio API.
- **Platform-agnostic types**: `AudioChunk` uses `Float32Array` arrays, compatible with both Node.js and browser environments.


---

## [Song editor](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/guide/editor/) (Guide)

---
title: "Song editor"
description: "Arrange vocal tracks, edit notes and expression, and save or render a song."
---

# Song editor

[Open the editor](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara). The starter phrase is ready to
play. Use **New** for an empty song or **Open** to load an existing file.

![The arrangement above the piano roll, with the track inspector on the left](/assets/images/editor.png)

## Tracks and parts

A track is a singer. Its inspector controls language, voice, level, and pan.
Mute and solo are available in the track header. **Add track** creates another
singer; the plus button in a track header adds a vocal part.

A part is a region of notes. Select it to open its notes in the piano roll. Drag
the part to move it in time, or onto another track to change its singer. Drag
the right edge to change its length.

The tempo field changes the initial tempo. Open the tempo/meter map beside it
to add changes later in the song. Map positions use project ticks: at the default
resolution, 480 ticks is one quarter note.

## Notes and lyrics

In **Notes** mode, click an empty space in the piano roll to add a note. Drag a
note to move it; drag its right edge to resize it. The snap control determines
the timing grid. Select **Off** for tick-level placement.

Select a note to edit its lyric, pitch, start, and length in the inspector.
Leave phonemes empty to use the track language's lyric conversion. Enter
space-separated phonemes to override that conversion for the note.

With the piano roll focused, **Delete** or **Backspace** removes the selected
note. Undo restores it.

## Pitch and expression

Switch to **Pitch** to add and move pitch points. Existing curves remain visible
in either mode, including on unselected notes. The selected note shows handles
for its points; a handle can be dragged beyond the note's vertical bounds.

![A selected note with pitch handles and editable intensity bars](/assets/images/expression.png)

Choose **Intensity** or **Velocity** in the expression lane below the piano roll.
Each bar spans a note's duration. Drag vertically to set its value, or drag across
several bars to edit a phrase. A completed drag is one undo step. **Escape**
cancels the current drag.

- Intensity ranges from 0 to 200%, with 100% as the default.
- Velocity ranges from 0 to 127, with 100 as the default.
- The numeric field edits the selected note exactly.
- With the lane focused, **Left/Right** selects notes in time order.
- **Up/Down** changes the value by 1; hold **Shift** for steps of 10.
- **Home/End** sets the value to its minimum or maximum.

## Playback and navigation

Press **Space** or click Play to start or pause playback. Stop returns the
playhead to the beginning. Both timelines can follow playback. Settings offers
**Page** follow, which advances at the viewport edge, and **Smooth** follow,
which moves the view with the playhead.

Scroll vertically to change the visible pitches. Scroll horizontally, or hold
**Shift** while scrolling, to move along the song. Hold **Cmd/Ctrl** while
scrolling to zoom. The toolbar also has zoom buttons.

## Save and export

**Save** or **Cmd/Ctrl+S** downloads an `.ichi` project. This is the format to keep
while editing: it retains tracks, parts, voices, phonemes, expression, tempo and
meter maps, and mix settings. Older `.ichikara` documents also open.

The browser keeps a recovery draft on this device, but it is not a substitute
for saving a file. Clearing browser storage removes the draft. Opening another
song asks what to do when the current song has unsaved changes.

Score import reads all tracks. Conversion may flatten source regions into one
part per track. USTX export includes all tracks at their song positions, but
does not preserve Ichikara voices, mix settings, or every expression field.
Meter changes must be on bar boundaries for score export; `.ichi` can retain
changes at other ticks.

WAV export renders the whole song in stereo with the current track mix. Choose
44.1 or 48 kHz in Settings before playback or export.

## Workspace settings

Drag a divider to resize the inspector, arrangement/piano split, expression
lane, track headers, or track rows. Focus a divider and use arrow keys for
keyboard resizing; **Home/End** moves it to its available limits.

Settings also controls the keyboard and expression lane visibility, default
snap, note height, selection color, and playback prebuffer. These preferences
stay on this device and do not change the song or its undo history.


---

## [Languages](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/guide/languages/) (Guide)

---
title: "Languages"
description: "Built-in language support and how to add custom languages"
---

## Built-in Languages

### English (en)

- **Phoneme set**: ARPAbet (39 phonemes: vowels, diphthongs, consonants)
- **G2P**: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (compressed, ~130k entries)
- **Fallback**: Character-level mapping for unknown words
- **Data sources**: Peterson & Barney 1952 (vowel formants), Jongman et al. 2000 (fricative spectra), Stevens 1998 (plosive/nasal data)

### Japanese (jp)

- **Phoneme set**: IPA-like (vowels a/i/u/e/o, consonants including moraic N)
- **G2P**: Hiragana and romaji parsing + EDICT2 kanji lookup
- **Pitch accent**: Automatic accent resolution for prosody generation
- **Data sources**: Yamada et al. 2019 (vowel formants), Kitamura et al. 2009 (F3), standard acoustic-phonetics lit

### Mandarin (zh)

- **Phoneme set**: Pinyin-derived (6 vowels, 21 consonants + apical vowels)
- **G2P**: Pinyin syllable decomposition with y/w spelling changes and tone stripping
- **Tone handling**: Tone numbers (1-5) are stripped from pinyin input; pitch contour is expected to be handled by note-level pitch bend in the score
- **Data sources**: Wu 1990 (standard Mandarin formant values), general acoustic phonetics

## Rests

A UTAU score marks a rest with an uppercase `R`. Every built-in language maps
that lyric to the `sil` phoneme, which is defined with `type: "silence"` and
`voiced: false`, so the note renders as true digital silence:

```typescript
renderScore(
  {
    tempos: [{ tick: 0, tempo: 120 }],
    resolution: 480,
    notes: [
      { tick: 0, lyric: "か", noteNum: 60, length: 480 },
      { tick: 480, lyric: "R", noteNum: 60, length: 480 }, // silence
      { tick: 960, lyric: "な", noteNum: 62, length: 480 },
    ],
  },
  voice,
  "jp",
);
```

The check is case-sensitive. Lowercase `r` stays singable, because it is a real
phoneme: the Japanese mora ら and the English approximant /ɹ/.

A custom language module must define `sil` as an unvoiced `silence` phoneme and
map the rest marker to it, or rests in imported scores will be sung.

## Using Language Modules

```typescript
import { japanese, english, mandarin, getLanguage } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

// Direct reference
renderScore(score, voice, japanese); // or "jp"

// String lookup
const lang = getLanguage("eng"); // returns english module
renderScore(score, voice, lang);
```

## Registering a Custom Language

Implement the `LanguageModule` interface and register it:

```typescript
import { registerLanguage } from "@audiflo/ichikara";
import type { LanguageModule, PhonemeDef } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const myLang: LanguageModule = {
  id: "custom",
  name: "My Language",
  phonemes: new Map([
    [
      "a",
      {
        symbol: "a",
        type: "vowel",
        voiced: true,
        formants: [
          { f: 800, bw: 100 },
          { f: 1200, bw: 150 },
          { f: 2500, bw: 200 },
          { f: 3500, bw: 250 },
          { f: 4500, bw: 300 },
        ],
      },
    ],
    // ... more phonemes
  ]),
  lyricToPhonemes(lyric: string): string[] {
    // Your G2P logic here
    return [...lyric].filter((ch) => this.phonemes.has(ch));
  },
};

registerLanguage(myLang);

// Now usable via "custom" string
const chunks = await renderScore(score, voice, "custom");
```

## Cross-Language Aliasing

The alias system maps language-specific phoneme symbols to a canonical IPA-like set. This is useful when a voicebank recorded for one language sings lyrics in another:

```typescript
import { toCanonical, sequenceToCanonical } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

// Map a single phoneme
toCanonical("en", "IY"); // -> "i"
toCanonical("jp", "sh"); // -> "S"

// Map a sequence
sequenceToCanonical("zh", ["zh", "ir"]);
// -> ["Z", "I"]
```


---

## [Renderer](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/guide/renderer/) (Guide)

---
title: "Renderer"
description: "How the synthesis engine produces audio from a score"
---

## Note Rendering Pipeline

When `renderNote()` processes a single note, it follows these steps:

### 1. Phoneme Resolution

The note's lyric string is passed to the language module's `lyricToPhonemes()` function, which returns an array of phoneme symbols:

```typescript
// Japanese: "こ" -> ["k", "o"]
// English:  "hello" -> ["HH", "AH", "L", "OW"]
// Mandarin: "ni3" -> ["n", "i"]  (tone stripped)
```

Each symbol is looked up in the language module's phoneme map to get a `PhonemeDef` with formant targets, noise parameters, duration defaults, and voicing state.

### 2. Duration Allocation

Phoneme durations are allocated from the note's total sample length:

- Consonants and silence get their `defaultDuration` (capped at 40% of the note)
- Vowels split the remaining time equally
- If the note is very short, all durations are scaled proportionally

### 3. Glottal Pulse Generation

For each sample, the LF glottal source computes a pulse based on:

- **F0**: base pitch from `noteNum`, modulated by pitch bend, vibrato, and accent
- **OQ/SQ/Tenseness**: from `VoiceConfig.glottal`
- **Jitter/Shimmer**: random cycle-to-cycle variation (adds natural instability)

The LF model produces the differentiated glottal flow: sinusoidal opening, a return phase with exponential decay modulated by a sinusoid for C1 continuity, and a closed phase (silence).

### 4. Formant Filtering

The glottal signal passes through a cascaded formant filter (anti-resonators first, then resonators, matching the source-filter model). Formant targets are interpolated:

- Between successive phonemes (cross-fade over ~30ms)
- Within diphthongs (sweep from onset to end formants)

Formant coefficients are updated at intervals of ~5ms to balance CPU usage against spectral accuracy.

### 5. Noise Mixing

Consonants add shaped noise:

- **Fricatives**: noise filtered through resonant peaks at the fricative's spectral centre
- **Plosives**: short noise burst with fast decay
- **Affricates**: a silent stop closure followed by a brief decaying release, so `ch` is not a sustained `sh`
- **Aspiration**: low-passed noise mixed into vowels (controlled by `glottal.aspiration`)

### 6. Envelope and Normalisation

Each phoneme gets a smooth amplitude envelope (attack/decay). The entire note is then normalised to prevent clipping, scaled by a gain factor derived from the peak sample.

## Cross-Note Continuity

The renderer returns both the `AudioChunk` and the final formant targets of the last phoneme. The streamer passes these as `prevFormants` to the next note, enabling smooth formant transitions across note boundaries.

## Performance

- Single-note rendering is O(n) in note duration
- The heaviest operations per sample are: glottal pulse computation, formant cascade (2 cascades × 5 filters each), and noise shaping
- For typical scores (tempo 120, 480 ticks/note), a note renders in under 1ms on modern hardware


---

## [Ichikara](https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara/docs/)

---
title: "Ichikara"
description: "A OneVoice song editor and TypeScript singing-synthesis library."
---

::: hero layout:split glow:true

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD025 -->

# Ichikara

Write and arrange songs in the browser, or synthesize singing from your own
TypeScript app. Ichikara generates voices from parameters rather than recorded
voicebanks.

::: tag "OneVoice Editor"
::: tag "LF Glottal"
::: tag "Cross-Language"

<!--markdownlint-disable MD034-->

::: button "Open Editor" external:https://audiflo.github.io/Ichikara icon:play
::: button "Quick Start" ./getting-started/quickstart.md icon:code

<!--markdownlint-disable MD034-->

::: button "GitHub" external:https://github.com/Audiflo/Ichikara icon:github

== side

::: card "OneVoice"
Choose a Chitose voice, then adjust its gender, breathiness, brightness, tension,
and vibrato. Each vocal track has its own voice and language. The same controls
are available through `scaleVoice()` in the library.
:::
:::

![Vocal tracks, piano-roll notes, and expression editing in Ichikara](assets/images/editor.png)

## Song editor

Arrange vocal parts across tracks, edit lyrics and phonemes, draw pitch curves,
and set intensity or velocity with note-length bars. Resize the workspace to
fit your song and follow playback in page or smooth mode.

Save as `.ichi` to retain voices, expression, parts, and mix settings. Export WAV
for audio or USTX to continue in another editor.

::: button "Editor Guide" ./guide/editor.md icon:music

## Features

::: grids
::: grid
::: card "LF Glottal Source" icon:waveform
Liljencrants-Fant glottal pulses with jitter, shimmer, aspiration noise, and DC
blocking. Control open quotient, speed quotient, tenseness, and power.
:::
:::

::: grid
::: card "Cascaded Formant Filter" icon:combine
Resonators and anti-resonators model the vocal tract, interpolating between
phoneme targets as the voice moves through a lyric.
:::
:::

::: grid
::: card "Three Languages" icon:globe
Japanese hiragana, romaji, and kanji; English text with CMUDict; and Mandarin
pinyin. Add another language through `registerLanguage`.
:::
:::

::: grid
::: card "Streaming Playback" icon:wind
Play chunks as they render through Web Audio. Native projects include track
placement, mute/solo, gain, and stereo pan.
:::
:::

::: grid
::: card "File Import / Export" icon:file-up
Read and write UST, USTX, VPR, VSQX, MIDI, MusicXML, and other score formats through
UtaFormatix. Keep an `.ichi` copy for native settings and region boundaries.
:::
:::

::: grid
::: card "OneVoice System" icon:sliders
Start with Chitose Chika, Sho, or Ren. Use the editor's voice controls or
`buildVoice()` and `scaleVoice()` to change the sound.
:::
:::
:::

## Quick Example

::: tabs

== tab "Node.js"

```typescript
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { renderScore, chitoseChika, encodeWav, type Score } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const score: Score = {
  tempos: [{ tick: 0, tempo: 120 }],
  resolution: 480,
  notes: [
    { lyric: "こ", noteNum: 60, length: 480 },
    { lyric: "ん", noteNum: 62, length: 480 },
    { lyric: "に", noteNum: 64, length: 480 },
    { lyric: "ち", noteNum: 65, length: 480 },
    { lyric: "は", noteNum: 67, length: 960 },
  ],
};

const chunks = await renderScore(score, chitoseChika, "jp");
writeFileSync("hello.wav", Buffer.from(encodeWav(chunks)));
```

== tab "Browser"

Call playback from a user action, using the score from the Node.js tab:

```typescript
import { streamScore, chitoseChika, StreamPlayer, type Score } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const player = new StreamPlayer();

async function playPhrase(score: Score): Promise<void> {
  await player.play(streamScore(score, chitoseChika, "jp"));
}
```

== tab "Custom Voice"

Pass this voice to `renderScore` or `streamScore` with your score and language:

```typescript
import { buildVoice, scaleVoice } from "@audiflo/ichikara";

const brightAlto = scaleVoice(
  buildVoice({
    name: "Bright Alto",
    formant: { scale: 1.25, shift: 2, bandwidth: 1.0 },
  }),
  {
    gender: 0.3,
    breathiness: 0.2,
    vibratoAmount: 0.8,
  },
);
```

:::

## Installation

```sh
npm install @audiflo/ichikara
```
